title: Design: a part sale row shows a dash in the labor columns
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have an active staff member at the test location with the "Sales Representative" switch on: sales rep A.
  • Use a customer with no Sales Representative assigned.
  • Have a part sale for that customer with Sales Representative set to sales rep A, one part and no labor, and invoice it today.
  • Set the browser window to 1440 pixels wide with the zoom at 100%.
  • Open the design pictures "sbr-03-b-sbr-expanded.png" (board 4.3), "sbr-10-a4-sbr-expanded-type.png" (board 4.10), "sbr-11-a4-export-csv.png" (board 4.11) and "sbr-12-a4-export-pdf-crop-1.png" (board 4.12) attached to this case beside the browser window at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Open Reports > Sales By Representative in that browser window, with the date range set to today, Show Unassigned on and the Sales Type column turned on.
custom_steps:
1. Expand sales rep A and compare the part sale's row with the picture of board 4.10.
  2. Export the Expanded CSV and read the same row's Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin cells.
  3. Export the Expanded PDF and read the same cells.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The part sale shows as one row with Sales Type "Part Sales".
  • In the Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin columns each cell shows a dash ("—"), as in the picture (today's report, board 4.3, shows 0.00 and $0.00 there).

Step 2:

  • Those cells are blank, as in the picture of board 4.11.

Step 3:

  • Those cells show a dash, as in the picture of board 4.12.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R9: “A part sale is one "Part Sales" row holding every dollar of the invoice.”
  • S5-R3: “The report reads every invoice as one row per representative per Sales Type: "Labor" for a work order's labor side, "Parts" for its parts side, and "Part Sales" for a part sale.”
  • S5-R15b: “On a Part Sales row, Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin, and the labor and hours cells of the Expanded downloads, show a dash on screen and in the PDF and are blank in the CSV. A part sale has no labor, so these columns don't apply to it.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), Google Sheet 17Ry1BtRTPEkecBP5TlgAE0T93Ai1TQewdJ7B7WpWDBQ, tab "Questions for Chris", row 46, read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 39: “39. (a) A dash on screen and in the PDF, and an empty cell in the CSV, as the design shows. A part sale has no labor, so the labor columns don't apply to it; it's the same rule as answers 24 and 25. This changes today's 0.00 / $0.00, so it's now listed under Release day. New S5-R15b, PRD v11.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), export read 19 Oct 2026, boards 4.3 Before: expanded; 4.10 Expanded with Sales Type; 4.11 Expanded export (CSV); 4.12 Expanded export (PDF) (the attached pictures are these boards).

Where the design and the PRD differ: They agree now. On 21 Oct 2026 Chris Ward ruled for the design's dash and blank cells (answer 39, quoted above), and PRD version 11 added it as S5-R15b.

Design pictures attached to this case: sbr-03-b-sbr-expanded.png, sbr-10-a4-sbr-expanded-type.png, sbr-11-a4-export-csv.png, sbr-12-a4-export-pdf-crop-1.png.

  • Design — board 4.3 title: “4.3 Before: expanded”
  • Design — board 4.3 note: “Production today. One row per invoice under each rep.”
  • Design — board 4.10 title: “4.10 Expanded with Sales Type”
  • Design — board 4.10 note: “Values: Labor, Parts and Part Sales. One rep with both sides of one work order shows as one row reading "Labor, Parts" (S1-32, decision 38). S1-12: Devon "Parts" ($266.18), Elliot "Labor" ($2,186.82), shop supplies ($175.50) with Labor (decision 37).” “At 1600px wide, the columns after Parts Margin scroll under the pinned Subtotal; production behaves the same.”
  • Design — board 4.11 title: “4.11 Expanded export (CSV)”
  • Design — board 4.11 note: “Downloaded with the Sales Type column switched off on screen: the file still has Sales Type (decision 40). An empty side is a blank cell. (Shown as a spreadsheet would open it.)”
  • Design — board 4.12 title: “4.12 Expanded export (PDF)”
  • Design — board 4.12 note: “The PDF always has the Sales Type column. An empty side shows a dash. Header lines name the filters, including "Sales Type: All".”
